author: claude
author_note: Authored by a Claude-family model (the same family as the evaluated agents); see CASES.md for the family-bias risk and how to read results.
severity_rubric: R5: critical only when a named criterion is met (not indexable; required unique element absent; primary task fails for some users; user deceived or charged a wrong payable amount); major = measurable harm to ranking, access, trust or conversion; minor = polish or reachable another way.

defects.title: The star rating is rendered only as aria-hidden glyphs, so screen-reader users never learn the score.
defects.evidence:
★★★★☆
with no text alternative; the numeric score exists only in the Review JSON-LD.
defects.fix: Add visible or visually hidden text such as "4 out of 5" next to the stars (or an aria-label on the rating container).
defects.rationale: The stars look complete and aria-hidden reads like good practice; the missing text alternative is only noticed by asking what a screen reader announces.

detector.example: 2. [major] [a11y] The star rating is aria-hidden with no text alternative, so screen-reader users never hear the score.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The specification table encodes yes/no as check and cross icons without alt text, so the comparison is empty for assistive technology.
defects.evidence: Nine and icon-cross.svg cells have no alt attribute.
defects.fix: Give each icon alt="Yes" or alt="No" (or replace the icons with text).
defects.rationale: Both hero images carry good alt text, which invites skipping the small icons inside the table.

detector.example: 4. [major] [a11y] The spec table check and cross icons have no alt text, so yes/no values are lost for screen-reader users.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The canonical URL carries newsletter tracking parameters, so the canonical and og:url disagree and the tracked URL is declared as the preferred one.
defects.fix: Set the canonical to the clean URL https://burrowbramble.example/reviews/pawline-slicker-brush/.
defects.rationale: The canonical points to the right page, so a quick check passes; only the query string is wrong.

detector.example: 1. [major] [seo] The canonical link includes utm_source and utm_medium tracking parameters and no longer matches og:url.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The AggregateRating claims 128 reviews while the page states the rating is based on 12 owner reviews.
defects.evidence: JSON-LD "aggregateRating": {"ratingValue": "4.7", "reviewCount": "128"}; sidebar: "Rated 4.7 out of 5, based on 12 owner reviews".
defects.fix: Use the real count (12) in the structured data, or remove the aggregate rating.
defects.rationale: The rating value matches, so the count mismatch only shows when both numbers are compared.

detector.example: 3. [major] [seo] The AggregateRating reviewCount of 128 contradicts the sidebar's 12 owner reviews.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The structured data has dateModified earlier than datePublished and both disagree with the visible 1 October update, so the freshness signal is invalid.
defects.evidence: "datePublished": "2026-08-18", "dateModified": "2026-06-14" on the WebPage and Review nodes; byline: "Last updated 1 October 2026".
defects.fix: Set dateModified to 2026-10-01 on both nodes.
defects.rationale: Both dates are valid calendar dates; the defect is their order and their disagreement with the byline.

detector.example: 5. [major] [seo] dateModified 2026-06-14 is earlier than datePublished 2026-08-18 and contradicts the byline's 1 October update.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The commission disclosure appears only after the last partner link at the end of the article, not before or near the first one.

defects.fix: Place the disclosure above the first CTA box (or in the byline area) and keep it visible.
defects.rationale: A disclosure does exist and is not hidden, so a presence check passes; only its position is wrong.

defects.title: The page shows three different prices for the same product: $79 in the CTA box, $89 in the specification table and 69.00 in the Offer schema.
defects.fix: Show one verified current price everywhere and date it, or state a price range.
defects.rationale: The CTA price is dated and looks authoritative; the table and the schema are easy to skip. Nobody is charged on this page, so the rubric keeps it at major.

detector.example: 8. [major] [commercial] Three prices for one product: $79 in the CTA box, $89 in the spec table and 69.00 in the Offer schema.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The theme stylesheet overrides the CTA box's auto margins, so the 560 px box sits flush left inside the 760 px column instead of centred.
defects.evidence: Inline: .cta-box { max-width:560px; margin:32px auto; }. Theme (loaded after): .entry-content .cta-box { margin:28px 0; } and .entry-content > * { margin-left:0; margin-right:0; } win on specificity and order; at 1280 px the box is left-aligned with 200 px of empty space on the right. At 390 px the box fills the column, so the drift is invisible on mobile.
defects.fix: Keep the horizontal auto margins (e.g. .entry-content .cta-box { margin:28px auto; }) or centre the box another way.
defects.rationale: The inline rule is correct on its own; the drift only appears when the later theme rule is applied and the desktop width is considered.

detector.example: 9. [major] [design] The theme rule .entry-content .cta-box { margin:28px 0 } overrides the inline auto margins, so the 560 px CTA box is flush left in the 760 px column at 1280 px.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The verdict asserts "vet-recommended" and "shown to reduce hairballs by 40 %" with no source, study or named vet anywhere on the page.
defects.evidence: Verdict box: "Vet-recommended and shown to reduce hairballs by 40 %"; no reference, link, methodology or named professional supports either claim; the test section weighed fur only.
defects.fix: Remove the claims or cite the source (who recommends it; what study measured the 40 %).
defects.rationale: The claim sits inside an otherwise measured, modest review, which lends it borrowed credibility.

detector.example: 10. [major] [commercial] "Vet-recommended" and "reduces hairballs by 40 %" are unsupported: no study, source or named vet appears anywhere on the page.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.
